elaine: Heads up: docs PR #492 is blocked on a runtime clarification. The config example uses `routing: preferred: 'redwood-7b', fallbacks: ['redwood-2b-quant']` and the reviewer flagged it for ambiguous behavior across hosted/dedicated/private. Also the Python streaming snippet implies `await stream.aclose()` will cancel server work immediately. Can infra or runtime owners confirm exact behavior so docs can be explicit? @samir @jon
samir: Quick ask  paste the exact snippet and the CI error. My short answer: hosted tries preferred then fallbacks in order; Dedicated may reject if `force_model_lock` is enabled and model missing. Private follows customer runtime. But nuances exist (tokenization differences, quantized variant limits). Need the exact text you plan to add.
elaine: Snippet from PR: ```
routing:
  preferred_model: "redwood-7b"
  fallback_models:
    - "redwood-2b-quant"
# Python streaming shown:
async with client.stream("/v1/generate", json=payload) as stream:
    async for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk)
    # cancels here with `await stream.aclose()`
```
CI note: docs-preview failed linkcheck for a fenced block in the same doc, fixed in branch, but we kept merge hold pending runtime wording.
jon: From runtime side: hosted routing uses the routing policy you describe. Dedicated respects `force_model_lock` on the pool: if true and the preferred model isn't available in that pool, we return 403 ModelUnavailable. If false, it falls back like hosted. Private is uncontrolled by us. Important callout: when falling back to a quantized or different-architecture model, tokenization may differ and the reported token counts in responses reflect the actual model used to serve the request, not the preferred model. That can surprise users when comparing costs.
maria: On SDK cancel: our Python streaming layer closes the client connection on `stream.aclose()` which results in TCP FIN. The server runtime receives that but may already be in a work batch; depending on batch/execute timing and cancellation polling, the server might finish generating the current request (and those tokens will be billed) before freeing resources. In short: client-side close != guaranteed immediate server abort.
tanya: Reviewer also asked whether this is purely docs wording or if we need an API change/deprecation. If behavior is unchanged and we're only clarifying, mark docs-only. If we want immediate hard-abort semantics, that's a runtime feature request and needs product/infra planning.
samir: I ran a small repro on staging: hosted -> preferred chosen, fallback used in order. Dedicated with pool missing preferred and `force_model_lock=true` -> 403. Dedicated with lock=false -> fallback works. For the SDK, cancelled clients still showed activity on the GPU for a short period before the runtime reclaimed memory.
elaine: Proposed doc sentences to paste into PR (want sign-off): "Routing behavior summary: Hosted: runtime attempts the preferred_model and, if unavailable, iterates fallback_models in order. Dedicated: behavior depends on pool setting `force_model_lock`; when true, requests for unavailable preferred models are rejected; when false, behavior matches Hosted. Private: subject to customer runtime configuration." And: "Note: Token counts and tokenization may differ between preferred and fallback models. The API's reported token usage corresponds to the model that actually served the request."
jon: LGTM besides one tweak: add explicit example of 403 text for `force_model_lock`. Suggest adding: "\"error\": {\"code\": \"ModelUnavailable\", \"message\": \"preferred model not present on this Dedicated pool\"}".
maria: For SDK cancel text: proposed: "Client-side stream close (e.g., `await stream.aclose()`) closes the HTTP connection but does not guarantee immediate termination of server-side execution. The server may continue producing tokens until the runtime processes cancellation; those tokens can be billed. To achieve hard-stop semantics, configure server-side execution timeouts or use Dedicated pools with explicit cancel policies."
tanya: Also add a tiny bullet matrix in the doc: Hosted / Dedicated (lock on/off) / Private with one-line behavior for each. Reviewer wants that.
elaine: I'll update the PR with the suggested wording and the 3-row bullet matrix. I fixed the fenced block causing linkcheck failure; CI re-run pending. Keeping the merge hold until you confirm the exact text is OK.
ci-bot: build/docs-preview #878 started: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/878
samir: Text looks good to me. Jon ok with error example?
jon: Yes. Also add a short sentence: "If your application requires strict billing predictability across model swaps, we recommend pinning to a single model (avoid fallbacks) or using Dedicated with `force_model_lock=true` and ensuring the model exists on the pool."
elaine: Added both notes and the example error payload. Re-running CI.
ci-bot: build/docs-preview #878 passed
elaine: CI passed, reviewer accepted wording. Removing merge hold and merging PR #492. Thank you all! :tada:
